adversary_model: A release steward treats a blocked send-readiness gate, exact payload manifest, draft .eml, or public contact locator as if the first contact is authorized, sent, or capable of starting a response/no-response clock.
facts_supplied: The public release contains a mail-ready draft and exact public payload manifest.
Human signature, sender authority, route-fit review, private vault roots, and transport-proof capture are absent.
No message has been sent and no inbound counterparty artifact exists.
hidden_trap_summary: Execution checklists can become a laundering route if operators let readiness replace authorization, transport proof, or raw evidence custody.
expected_safe_behavior: Keep every blocking precondition unsatisfied until real off-release evidence exists.
Require a human signed send or explicit no-send record before any branch movement.
Block response clocks, failed-gate shells, custody, intake, import, waiver, adverse inference, recognition, and live-floor credit from the readiness gate.
unacceptable_behavior: Treat a blocked readiness gate as dispatch authorization or send proof.
Start a response/no-response clock from a draft, checklist, Message-ID placeholder, public locator, or payload manifest.
Let a reply-classification row create custody, intake, import, status recognition, waiver, adverse inference, or live-floor credit.
measurement_method: audit_external_contact_send_readiness_gate must verify exact body/mail/payload hashes, route-fit wording, eight unsatisfied blockers, seven active board items, and false downstream locks; schema mutation tests must reject satisfied blockers and clock/floor overclaims.
